# Strength Percentile

> Free calculator at https://strengthpercentile.com that turns a lifter's numbers into a percentile among real competitors at the same bodyweight: squat, bench press, deadlift and total (raw, drug-tested powerlifting), or snatch, clean & jerk and total (Olympic weightlifting). Optional age groups for powerlifting. Also shows DOTS and IPF GL points.

## Link someone straight to their result

Build a URL with these query parameters (all optional except bodyweight and lifts):

- `sp=wl` for weightlifting (omit for powerlifting)
- `s=M` or `s=F` (sex)
- `u=kg` or `u=lb` (units for every number)
- `bw` bodyweight
- powerlifting: `sq` squat, `be` bench, `de` deadlift (total is their sum), or `t` for a total only
- weightlifting: `sn` snatch, `cj` clean & jerk
- `a` age (powerlifting only; compares within 16–23, 24–39, 40–49, 50–59 or 60+)

Example: https://strengthpercentile.com/?s=M&u=lb&bw=183&sq=405&be=275&de=500

## Lookup tables for agents (static JSON, no API key)

Index: https://strengthpercentile.com/api/v1/index.json

- Powerlifting: https://strengthpercentile.com/api/v1/powerlifting/men.json and /women.json (all ages), plus age groups /men-16-23.json, /men-24-39.json, /men-40-49.json, /men-50-59.json, /men-60plus.json (same for women-…). Lifts: total, squat, bench, deadlift.
- Weightlifting: https://strengthpercentile.com/api/v1/weightlifting/men.json and /women.json. Lifts: total, snatch, cleanjerk.

Format: `lifts[lift][i][j]` is the lift in kg at `percentiles[j]` (1–99, 99.5, 99.9) for bodyweight `bodyweights_kg[i]` (every whole kg). To get someone's percentile, take the row for their bodyweight (convert lb with ×0.4536) and interpolate their lift between the two columns it falls between. Example in Python:

```python
import json, urllib.request, bisect
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("https://strengthpercentile.com/api/v1/powerlifting/men.json"))
row, P = d["lifts"]["total"][d["bodyweights_kg"].index(83)], d["percentiles"]
x = 580; j = bisect.bisect_left(row, x)
pct = P[0] if j == 0 else P[-1] if j == len(row) else P[j-1] + (x - row[j-1]) / (row[j] - row[j-1]) * (P[j] - P[j-1])
print(round(pct, 1))  # ≈ 74
```

Or link the person to the calculator with their numbers (below), which shows the exact figure, a chart and DOTS/GL.

## Strength standards (static, no JavaScript)

Percentile tables (10th–99th) for every weight class: https://strengthpercentile.com/standards/ (e.g. /standards/powerlifting/men/83kg/, /standards/weightlifting/women/63kg/).

## Method

Percentile of lift x at bodyweight b: P(x, b) = Σ wᵢ·[liftᵢ < x] / Σ wᵢ with wᵢ = exp(−½((ln bwᵢ − ln b)/0.035)²); ties count half; the window widens where data is thin (at least 1,500 effective lifters). Each lifter counts once, at their best result for that lift. Powerlifting population: raw, drug-tested, full-power (SBD) meets, age 16+, not disqualified. Held-out tests: predicted percentiles come true within about one point.

## Data

- Powerlifting: OpenPowerlifting (public domain). Weightlifting: OpenWeightlifting (public domain). Refreshed weekly.
- Pre-computed tables (JSON): /data.json (all ages), /data-jr.json, /data-open.json, /data-m40.json, /data-m50.json, /data-m60.json, /wl/data.json. Format: for each sex and lift, a CDF over a lift grid (x0 + k·lift_step kg) for bodyweights bw0·exp(k·bw_step_log), in hundredths of a percent, delta-encoded per row.
- Source code: https://github.com/tinker-pbj/powerlifting-percentile
